title: I Took the Worm-Bin Moisture Log to the Chair Who Left My Numbered Bedding

parts.text: I stepped into the worm shed at 8:07 a.m. and chair Dot was already using numbered gear. The board said: ONE BIN. THIRTY MINUTES. BEDDING STAYS WITH THE LOG. I was thirty, garden secretary, holding a clipboard that listed our numbered bedding. Dot shrugged. "Chairs are the worms." I photographed the board, the booking, and her leftover castings scoop on my numbered bedding. Then I asked for the moisture log. At 8:15 the shed pinged why Dot's name was on my scoop. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The shed can see Dot's leftover castings scoop on my numbered bedding.

social.video_title: She left my numbered worm bedding on my bin — Part 1/2
social.description: Worm shed, leftover scoop, a thirty-minute clock she posted. I logged the moisture. Would you have asked for the moisture log?

parts.text: Dot called it harvest until the shed asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the scoop still. The bedding went back to my numbered log. Dot ran a slot of her own and told the next chair atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: CHAIRS ARE NOT THE WORMS. I keep my bedding in a labeled sack. Dot brown-bags her harvest. The shed finally looks like a log, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Chairs are not the worms — Part 2/2
social.description: Moisture log, numbered bedding, and a second line on the board. Was harvest ever my scoop?
